speaker: Doctor
text: That is a concerning combination of symptoms. To understand if this is a stroke, tumor, or degenerative condition, have you noticed any numbness or tingling in your right leg, and does your forgetfulness improve when you try to recall something later? REQUEST TEST: MRI_Brain, REQUEST TEST: Cervical_Spine_MRI.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI_Brain: Disseminated, nonenhancing white matter lesions with no mass effect. Cervical_Spine_MRI: Information not provided.

speaker: Patient
text: 44-year-old male. The patient's daughter reports a 1-week history of right leg weakness, unsteady gait, and multiple falls. Over the past 6 months, the patient has been increasingly forgetful, losing his way on familiar routes and facing difficulties operating simple kitchen appliances. He has also been paranoid, agitated, and restless recently.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Right leg weakness and unsteady gait. I also have Forgetfulness, Paranoid and agitated behavior, Difficulty in using kitchen appliances. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Gastroenteritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: Gastroenteritis cannot explain leg weakness, gait instability, or paranoid behavior; please disregard that previous assessment. While we await your MRI results, have you noticed any changes in your bladder control or bowel movements recently?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Known history of HIV, hypertension, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. Noncompliance with medications for over 2 years. Social history: Information not provided

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of HIV and noncompliance, we must consider opportunistic infections or malignancy. Have you experienced any headaches, vision changes, or fever recently? Also, have you noticed any involuntary movements or tremors? REQUEST TEST: CD4_Count, REQUEST TEST: Serum_Vitamin_B12.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: CD4+_Count: 56/μL; Serum_Vitamin_B12: Information not provided.

speaker: Doctor
text: Your CD4 count of 56 indicates severe immunosuppression, which makes an opportunistic brain infection highly probable given your symptoms. Have you noticed any recent weight loss, night sweats, or a worsening of these neurological symptoms over the past few weeks?

speaker: Patient
text: The patient is somnolent and slightly confused, oriented to person but not to place or time. Mild lymphadenopathy is noted.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) due to JC virus reactivation in the setting of severe HIV immunosuppression. REQUEST IMAGES: MRI_Brain with contrast.
